plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 23: Gauss's Law
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of a cube sitting in the uniform field between two oppositely charged plates. Two large grey parallelograms are drawn in perspective, one above and one below, labeled '-q' at the right edge of the upper plate and '+q' at the right edge of the lower one; both are covered with short red arrows that all point straight up, and the field itself is named with a vector E at the far left. Between the plates stands a cube with every vertex lettered, A, B, C and D around the bottom face and F, G, H and K around the top, so the bottom face reads ABCD and the top face FGHK. A shaded diagonal plane is drawn inside the cube, running from the upper edge KF down to the lower edge BC and dividing the cube into two wedges. Red field arrows continue through the cube's interior, entering the bottom face and leaving the top face, while the four vertical side faces lie parallel to them. Because the identical arrows enter below and exit above, the reader is meant to tally signed contributions face by face and see them cancel. The arrangement is used to evaluate the flux through a closed surface that encloses no charge.

large upper negatively charged conducting plate drawn as a light gray horizontal parallelogram above the cube
thin dark outlines around both plates
label '+q' at the right edge of the lower plate
label '-q' at the right edge of the upper plate

many identical red electric-field arrows distributed over the upper plate, all pointing vertically upward
several red electric-field arrows passing through the space between plates and through the cube interior
vector label E with arrow notation at the left side of the field
transparent wireframe cube centered between the plates
subtle transparent cube faces so the cube reads as a closed Gaussian surface
bottom cube face ABCD
top cube face FGHK
four vertical side faces ABGF, BCHG, CDKH, and DAFK
cube vertex labels A, B, C, D on the lower face
cube vertex labels F, G, H, K on the upper face
semi-transparent diagonal interior plane spanning top edge KF to lower edge BC
click-selectable highlight overlay for the chosen cube face

interactions.teaches: A learner identifies which cube faces have outward normals aligned with, opposite to, or perpendicular to the electric field, so signed flux is built face by face rather than guessed from the picture

interactions.label: Flux view
interactions.teaches: Switching from individual contributions to the combined total shows that the field entering through the bottom face and leaving through the top face cancels to zero net flux
Rotating the scene makes clear that the electric field is perpendicular to the top and bottom faces but parallel to every side face

demo_steps.title: Face-by-face flux
demo_steps.narration: Click the bottom face ABCD, the top face FGHK, or any vertical side face. The selected outward normal appears, and the sign of E dot n shows whether the field enters, leaves, or merely skims that face.

demo_steps.title: Net flux cancellation
demo_steps.narration: The top face contributes +EA while the bottom face contributes -EA. The side faces contribute zero, so the total flux through the closed cube is zero.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a cube of side length L = 2 world units. Define cube coordinates with +X screen-right along AB and FG, +Y vertical upward along AF, BG, CH, DK, and +Z the receding diagonal along AD, BC, FK, GH. Place A=(-1,0,-1), B=(1,0,-1), C=(1,0,1), D=(-1,0,1), F=(-1,2,-1), G=(1,2,-1), H=(1,2,1), K=(-1,2,1). The cube should sit midway between two horizontal plates. Lower plate: centered near (0,-1.25,0), size about 7.0 × 4.6 in X × Z, very thin, light gray #d8d8d8 with dark gray #777777 outline, label '+q' on its right edge. Upper plate: centered near (0,3.25,0), same size and orientation, label '-q' on its right edge. Field arrows are red #c9363c, vertical +Y, with short shafts and cone heads; distribute them in regular staggered rows on both plates and a smaller set through the cube. The electric field is uniform: E = E0 y-hat. Set E0 = 1 for displayed formulas. Top face FGHK has outward normal +y and flux +E0 L^2 = +4E0. Bottom face ABCD has outward normal -y and flux -E0 L^2 = -4E0. All four side faces have normals perpendicular to y-hat and flux 0. The diagonal interior plane is the quadrilateral K-F-B-C, semi-transparent pale cyan/gray #b7d7d7 at about 0.45 opacity, with a soft white specular highlight; it runs from the upper left/top edge KF down diagonally to the lower right/front edge BC as in the source.
interactionPlan.notes: Render plates as semi-transparent double-sided PlaneGeometry or very thin boxes so they remain visible from the axonometric view. Use InstancedMesh for the repeated red arrows. Keep labels as screen-facing text sprites with slight depth offset to avoid z-fighting. In Face sum view, clicking ABCD should tint the face red/orange and draw a downward normal arrow labeled n outward, with annotation E·n < 0 and Phi_ABCD = -EA. Clicking FGHK should tint green/blue and draw an upward normal arrow with Phi_FGHK = +EA. Clicking any side face should tint neutral gray and draw a horizontal outward normal with Phi_side = 0 because E is parallel to the face. In Net flux view, show persistent top and bottom colored contribution tags and the equation Phi_net = (+EA) + (-EA) + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0.

authoredContext:
The figure shows the electric field of an oppositely charged, parallel-plate system and an imaginary box between the plates. The electric field between the plates is uniform and points from the positive plate toward the negative plate. A calculation of the flux of this field through various faces of the box shows that the net flux through the box is zero. Why does the flux cancel out here?

Electric flux through a cube, placed between two charged plates. Electric flux through the bottom face (ABCD) is negative, because E→ is in the opposite direction to the normal to the surface. The electric flux through the top face (FGHK) is positive, because the electric field and the normal are in the same direction. The electric flux through the other faces is zero, since the electric field is perpendicular to the normal vectors of those faces. The net electric flux through the cube is the sum of fluxes through the six faces. Here, the net flux through the cube is equal to zero. The magnitude of the flux through rectangle BCKF is equal to the magnitudes of the flux through both the top and bottom faces.

A cube ABCDKFGH is shown in the center. A diagonal plane is shown within it from KF to BC. The top surface of the cube, FGHK has a plane labeled minus q slightly above it and parallel to it. Similarly, another plane is labeled plus q is shown slightly below the bottom surface of the cube, parallel to it. Small red arrows are shown pointing upwards from the bottom plane, pointing up to the bottom surface of the cube, pointing up from the top surface of the cube and pointing up to the top plane. These are labeled vector E.

The reason is that the sources of the electric field are outside the box. Therefore, if any electric field line enters the volume of the box, it must also exit somewhere on the surface because there is no charge inside for the lines to land on. Therefore, quite generally, electric flux through a closed surface is zero if there are no sources of electric field, whether positive or negative charges, inside the enclosed volume. In general, when field lines leave (or “flow out of”) a closed surface, Φ is positive; when they enter (or “flow into”) the surface, Φ is negative.

plan.contextChunk: This figure is a three-dimensional diagram of a cube sitting in the uniform field between two oppositely charged plates. Two large grey parallelograms are drawn in perspective, one above and one below, labeled '-q' at the right edge of the upper plate and '+q' at the right edge of the lower one; both are covered with short red arrows that all point straight up, and the field itself is named with a vector E at the far left. Between the plates stands a cube with every vertex lettered, A, B, C and D around the bottom face and F, G, H and K around the top, so the bottom face reads ABCD and the top face FGHK. A shaded diagonal plane is drawn inside the cube, running from the upper edge KF down to the lower edge BC and dividing the cube into two wedges. Red field arrows continue through the cube's interior, entering the bottom face and leaving the top face, while the four vertical side faces lie parallel to them. Because the identical arrows enter below and exit above, the reader is meant to tally signed contributions face by face and see them cancel. The arrangement is used to evaluate the flux through a closed surface that encloses no charge.

interactions.teaches: A learner identifies which cube faces have outward normals aligned with, opposite to, or perpendicular to the electric field, so signed flux is built face by face rather than guessed from the picture

interactions.label: Flux view
interactions.teaches: Switching from individual contributions to the combined total shows that the field entering through the bottom face and leaving through the top face cancels to zero net flux
Rotating the scene makes clear that the electric field is perpendicular to the top and bottom faces but parallel to every side face

demo_steps.title: Face-by-face flux
demo_steps.narration: Click the bottom face ABCD, the top face FGHK, or any vertical side face. The selected outward normal appears, and the sign of E dot n shows whether the field enters, leaves, or merely skims that face.

demo_steps.title: Net flux cancellation
demo_steps.narration: The top face contributes +EA while the bottom face contributes -EA. The side faces contribute zero, so the total flux through the closed cube is zero.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use a cube of side length L = 2 world units. Define cube coordinates with +X screen-right along AB and FG, +Y vertical upward along AF, BG, CH, DK, and +Z the receding diagonal along AD, BC, FK, GH. Place A=(-1,0,-1), B=(1,0,-1), C=(1,0,1), D=(-1,0,1), F=(-1,2,-1), G=(1,2,-1), H=(1,2,1), K=(-1,2,1). The cube should sit midway between two horizontal plates. Lower plate: centered near (0,-1.25,0), size about 7.0 × 4.6 in X × Z, very thin, light gray #d8d8d8 with dark gray #777777 outline, label '+q' on its right edge. Upper plate: centered near (0,3.25,0), same size and orientation, label '-q' on its right edge. Field arrows are red #c9363c, vertical +Y, with short shafts and cone heads; distribute them in regular staggered rows on both plates and a smaller set through the cube. The electric field is uniform: E = E0 y-hat. Set E0 = 1 for displayed formulas. Top face FGHK has outward normal +y and flux +E0 L^2 = +4E0. Bottom face ABCD has outward normal -y and flux -E0 L^2 = -4E0. All four side faces have normals perpendicular to y-hat and flux 0. The diagonal interior plane is the quadrilateral K-F-B-C, semi-transparent pale cyan/gray #b7d7d7 at about 0.45 opacity, with a soft white specular highlight; it runs from the upper left/top edge KF down diagonally to the lower right/front edge BC as in the source.
interactionPlan.notes: Render plates as semi-transparent double-sided PlaneGeometry or very thin boxes so they remain visible from the axonometric view. Use InstancedMesh for the repeated red arrows. Keep labels as screen-facing text sprites with slight depth offset to avoid z-fighting. In Face sum view, clicking ABCD should tint the face red/orange and draw a downward normal arrow labeled n outward, with annotation E·n < 0 and Phi_ABCD = -EA. Clicking FGHK should tint green/blue and draw an upward normal arrow with Phi_FGHK = +EA. Clicking any side face should tint neutral gray and draw a horizontal outward normal with Phi_side = 0 because E is parallel to the face. In Net flux view, show persistent top and bottom colored contribution tags and the equation Phi_net = (+EA) + (-EA) + 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 0.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click for selecting a cube face: the learner clicks ABCD, FGHK, or a side face, the chosen face normal and E dot n contribution appear with positive, negative, or zero color coding, making signed electric flux a face-by-face sum.
- Toggle between face-sum and net-flux views: the learner switches views, the individual top and bottom contributions are shown separately and then combined to zero, clarifying why equal field entering and leaving means no enclosed charge.

discrepancies: The cube/camera orientation differs noticeably from the source, making several vertex labels appear on different visible corners than in the textbook figure.
Vertex labels are not faithfully placed: A and C in particular appear shifted toward interior/front positions rather than the corresponding bottom cube corners shown in the source.
The generated electric-field arrows inside the cube are much denser and more visually cluttered than the source, partially obscuring the cube and diagonal plane.
The upper and lower plate composition is more compressed around the cube than in the source, where the plates are larger and more separated vertically in the page layout.
The cube faces are rendered with extra pale transparent face surfaces and interactive highlight machinery not present in the original static figure.
